# Finance

The Township of Spallumcheen Finance Department is responsible for the financial administration of the Township and provides a number of services directly to residents, business, and community organizations. 

The Finance Department is responsible for:

 Accounts payable and accounts receivable  |  Business Licences
Cemetery Administration
 |  Climate Action - Emissions Reporting
Financial reporting and annual financial statements 
 |  Five-Year Financial Plan and annual budget preparation 
  Grant-In-Aid
 |  Parks and Recreation financial administration
 Permissive tax exemptions
 |  Property taxation and tax collection
 Special event permits  |  Water Utility billing and administration
 

## Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable

The Township prepares between 1100 and 1200 payments annually totaling in excess of $5,000,000.00. Payments are issued at middle and end of each month.

## Business Licences

The Finance Department administers Township business licences, including new applications, annual renewals, and Inter-Community Business Licences. 

Businesses operating within the Township may require a valid business licence before commencing operations. 

For application forms, fees, and licencing requirements, please visit Business Licencing

## Cemetery Administration

The Finance Department administrative services for the Armstrong-Spallumcheen Cemetery located at 4320 Highland Park Road. For more information please review the Cemetery page.

## Climate Action Emissions Reporting

2018 CARIP Climate Action/Carbon Neutral Progress Survey

## Financial Reporting and Annual Financial Statements

The Township prepares annual financial statements in accordance with Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards. The financial statements are independently audited and presented to Council each year. 

The audited financial statements of the Township of Spallumcheen must be accepted by the Township Council before June 30th in the subsequent year. Also required is the report on Council’s remuneration and expenses, and reports on supplier payments and employee earnings.

The Township also prepares statutory financial reports, including reports relating to Council remuneration and expenses, employee remuneration and supplier payments. These reports are included in the Annual Report . 

## Five-Year Financial Plan and Annual Budget

Each year, the Township prepares a Five-Year Financial Plan that establishes anticipated revenues, operating expenditures and capital expenditures for Township Services. 

The financial Planning process includes opportunities for public input before Council considers adoption of the Financial Plan and annual Tax Rates Bylaws.

Current Financial Plans, budgets and related financial information are available through the links below:

2026-2030 Consolidated Financial Plan Bylaw No. 2187, 2026

## Grants in Aid

The Township of Spallumcheen accepts applications for Grants-in-Aid annually no later than July 31st in each year. Reporting requirements required to be submitted with the application are outlined in the Township of Spallumcheen Grants-in-Aid Policy #1850.001, which is available at the municipal Office at 4144 Spallumcheen Way, Spallumcheen, BC during regular business hours, or on this site highlighted below.

# Financial Plans and Reports

Section Menu

The District of Sooke’s financial plans and reports provide a transparent look at how public funds are managed to deliver community services, maintain infrastructure, and plan for the future.

Each year, Council adopts a Five-Year Financial Plan that outlines the District’s revenues, expenses, and capital investments. This plan is updated annually to reflect current priorities, service levels, and community needs.

The annual Budget Process engages residents in setting priorities and understanding how tax dollars support services such as roads, parks, protective services, and community development. Stay informed about the annual budget process at letstalk.sooke.ca/budget.

Explore Documents

Access detailed financial documents in one searchable location. Use the tool below to find plans, reports, and statements that outline how the District of Sooke manages public funds, plans infrastructure investments, and delivers community services.

Documents are searchable by year and type, making it easy to view the Five-Year Financial Plan, Annual Report, Audited Financial Statements, and other financial resources.

# Freedom of Information and Privacy

Section Menu

The District of Sooke is committed to openness, transparency, and the protection of personal privacy.

We collect, use, and disclose information in accordance with the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA). This legislation ensures that the public has the right to access most records held by the District, while also safeguarding personal information from unauthorized use or disclosure.

Accessing Information

Most information about District operations is available online — including Council and Committee meeting documents, bylaws, policies, and financial reports. Before making a formal request, check the District website or contact us to see if the information you need is already publicly available.

If the records you’re looking for are not available online, you can submit a Freedom of Information (FOI) request.

Freedom of Information Requests

Under the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA), you have the right to request access to most records held by the District of Sooke.

#### Formal Requests

If the information you are seeking is not available through regular channels, you may submit a formal Freedom of Information (FOI) request. Formal requests must be made in writing and should clearly describe the records being requested. Providing specific details, such as relevant subjects, dates, or departments, will help staff locate and retrieve the records more efficiently.
